label: Anomaly detection on seasonal metrics
summary: A runnable reference for detecting anomalies in operational metrics: a rolling z-score, a robust seasonal baseline and a calendar-aware version, judged by recall, detection delay and false alerts per series per week at a fixed alert budget.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 10 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints 120 series by 2,016 hours with about 335 anomalies and 2.7% of points inside benign calendar events. baseline.py reports, at an alert budget of 0.5 false alerts per series per week tuned on the first 60% of time, a rolling z-score recall of 0.48, a seasonal baseline recall of 0.89 (but 0.78 false alerts on held-out time, over budget) and the calendar-aware seasonal detector recall of 0.95 at 0.50 false alerts. pytest reports 7 passed.

files.purpose: Synthetic hourly series with daily and weekly seasonality, three anomaly shapes and benign calendar events
Rolling z-score, seasonal robust z-score, calendar-aware suppression, alert policy and the event-level evaluation
Executable gates: determinism, no-future scores, refractory period, evaluation arithmetic and the detector comparison

synthetic.description: 120 hourly series over 12 weeks with level, daily and weekly seasonality and noise; about 2.8 anomalies per series (spikes, level shifts and slow drifts) and several benign calendar events per series that move the level on purpose.
knobs: n_series, weeks: size of the panel (defaults 120 and 12)
anomalies_per_series: average number of real anomalies
seed: identical seed gives an identical panel

slots.meaning: value minus the median of the same hour of the same weekday in previous weeks
median absolute deviation of recent residuals
known events that are supposed to move the level
persistence of a deviation over several hours
quiet time after an alert so one event raises one alert

data.threshold: pytest -k deterministic passes; anomalies between 0.5% and 8% of points and benign calendar events above 1%
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: Corrupting every value after hour t (set to 1,000,000) changes no score before t (maximum absolute difference 0)

baseline.metric: Recall and false alerts at the alert budget
baseline.threshold: Rolling z-score recorded as the number to beat (the kit: recall 0.48 at 0.27 false alerts per series-week)

challenger.metric: Recall gain at the same budget
challenger.threshold: Calendar-aware seasonal detector recall at least 0.30 above the rolling z-score with false alerts at most 0.6 per series-week on held-out time (the kit: 0.95 at 0.50)

tests.pass: Setting every value after the cut-off to a huge number changes no earlier score
Consecutive threshold crossings produce one alert and alerts are at least 6 hours apart
Recall, detection delay and false alerts per series-week match a hand-computed example
Recall at least 0.30 higher at the alert budget
Calendar-aware detector has no more false alerts than the plain seasonal one and at least its recall

lessons.evidence: A rolling z-score finds 48% of events at the alert budget; a seasonal baseline finds 89%.
Without the calendar the seasonal detector has 0.78 false alerts per series-week on held-out time against a budget of 0.5; with it, 0.50 at higher recall.

lessons.trap: Tuning the threshold on the data you report
lessons.evidence: Thresholds are chosen on the first 60% of time and reported on the last 40%, where the plain seasonal detector drifts over budget.

lessons.trap: A rolling window that includes the present
lessons.evidence: The no-future test corrupts everything after hour t and requires earlier scores to be unchanged.

target: A point is anomalous when it lies inside an anomaly interval. An event is detected when an alert fires inside the interval (or up to 3 hours after); delay is measured from the interval's start.

headline.baseline: recall 0.48 at 0.27 false alerts per series-week (rolling z-score)
